about: vercel's decision table (the P3 procedure). The manifest keys its resources by their stored names, so the derived core claims no operation: every served operation is a handler, the World's acts outside the API are doors, and the dashboard pages and the Edge Config read host are screens (the manifest's screens). Every other operation of the document is the gap.

decisions.demand: Dub's custom domains (a new domain, a renamed one, the admin's refresh, a claimed .link domain)
decisions.why: a create the document types inline: the project domain keyed by its project and name, its apex made the team's, verified unless another Vercel account holds the apex (then a TXT verification challenge), and the account's own domain refused 409 domain_already_in_use; the customer entry's addDomainToVercel (first-use.json domains.mjs) asserts the added domain's name, apex, project and verified

decisions.demand: Dub's domain status and its hourly verification cron (the *.apex wildcard first)
decisions.why: a read of a project domain by its project and name, the composite key the core does not address by the path; a missing one 404 not_found; the customer entry (first-use.json domains.mjs) looks up the apex's wildcard first (not found) and its readback reads the domain verified on its project

decisions.demand: Dub's domain status and its hourly verification cron (the *.apex wildcard first)
decisions.why: computed: how Vercel sees the domain's DNS (a Vercel zone its registrar delegates, or the owner's CNAME or A record at their DNS host), no stored answer; the customer entry (first-use.json domains.mjs) asserts the new domain misconfigured with Vercel's recommended CNAME

decisions.demand: Dub's verify route, retried until verified
decisions.why: a state move (verified false to true) that holds only when the challenge's TXT record is set at the owner's DNS host; refused 400 missing_txt_record otherwise

decisions.demand: Dub's removal of a domain while another under its apex is in use, and the admin's refresh
decisions.why: a delete under the composite key; the team's apex domain stays

decisions.demand: Dub's removal of the only domain in use under its apex
decisions.why: a delete of the team domain that takes the project domains under it (Deleting a domain will automatically remove any associated aliases), answered with its uid

decisions.demand: Dub's configureVercelNameservers for a bought .link domain
decisions.why: op update with zone: the domain's zone state, served by Vercel's DNS once true; op move-out is not demanded; zone: false, which no application sends, is the manifest's variant, answered as the gap

decisions.demand: Dub's updateConfig, which adds to its blocklists on a ban
decisions.why: a batch of item writes (create, update, upsert, delete), each item one subject, refused whole when one is refused, and the store's digest and item count kept for the read host; the customer entry (first-use.json domains.mjs) writes Dub's blocklists, then bans a domain by writing the item back

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed root's refresh of project domains (the manifest's refresh scope, once per project)
decisions.why: a list of a project's domains under the composite key, paged by time (pagination next and prev), filtered by verified and redirect as the document says

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed root's refresh of projects (the manifest's refresh scope)
decisions.why: the team's projects under Vercel's projects envelope with its pagination, which the manifest's list model does not write

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed root's refresh of team domains (the manifest's refresh scope)
decisions.why: the team's domains under Vercel's domains envelope with its pagination (20 unless a limit is asked)

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed root's refresh of teams (the manifest's refresh scope)
decisions.why: the teams a token reaches: a team-scoped token's own team, under the teams envelope

decisions.demand: the vendor-backed root's refresh of Edge Configs (the manifest's refresh scope)
decisions.why: every Edge Config of the team in one unpaged list (spec/patches.json: the answer is a list)

decisions.demand: the life's premise: Inês's Vercel account and Pro team, which the dashboard sign-in and Account Tokens page act for
decisions.why: a person signs up to Vercel on its website; the API makes no account

decisions.demand: the dashboard's sign-in, whose one-time password Vercel emails
decisions.why: an email Vercel sent a person is read in their inbox, not through the API

decisions.demand: the life's premise: the project Vercel made when the team imported its Git repository
decisions.why: the applications' project is made on the dashboard by the Git import (Deploying is Vercel's Git integration in every application), never by their API calls

decisions.demand: the runtime's credential door (the descriptor's credentialDoor): Dub's VERCEL_API_KEY, TEAM_ID_VERCEL, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, EDGE_CONFIG and EDGE_CONFIG_ID, Cal.com's EDGE_CONFIG
decisions.why: a token, a project and an Edge Config's connection string are made on the dashboard (Account Tokens, the Git import, Storage); the door issues them to a World's applications as their owner would

decisions.demand: Dub's .link domains, whose nameservers point at Vercel's at the registrar
decisions.why: a domain's nameservers are set at its registrar, outside Vercel

decisions.demand: Dub's customers' CNAME, A and TXT records, which getDomainConfig and verifyProjectDomain read
decisions.why: a record a domain's owner sets at their own DNS host is outside Vercel

decisions.demand: Dub's verification challenge, asked for only when another Vercel account holds the apex
decisions.why: another account's hold on a domain is that account's, not the caller's API to make

decisions.demand: Vendor-backed refresh of Edge Config items (manifest refresh scope).
decisions.why: The vendor returns every item as an array, scoped to its team's Edge Config, stored one subject per key.

decisions.demand: The vendor's published item-update example and canonical path used by blind adoption.
decisions.why: The canonical Global Config path and Dub's Edge Config path share the same stored mutation and response.
